newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Acom to launch credit firm in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Acom to launch credit firm in Thailand.

text.p: Acom Co Ltd said on Friday that it plans to launch a credit joint venture in early October in Thailand as the company's first overseas operation.
The joint venture, Siam A&C Co Ltd, will be established with starting capital of 120 million baht (522 million yen) and is expected to start operating in November, an Acom statement said.
Acom is a major consumer financing company in Japan.
The venture will finance the purchase of goods by consumers using an installment plan.
It will be 10 percent owned by Acom and 32 percent by five local firms which belong to or are closely associated with the Karnchanachari financial group, the statement said.

The Thai units of three Japanese companies -- Yaohan Japan Corp, Itochu Corp and Omron Corp -- will also hold a total of 19 percent, while the remaining 39 percent will be held by a Singapore joint venture between Acom and Yaohan, the statement said.
Acom said it expected the business to be profitable due to Thailand's rapid economic growth and an emerging middle class.
